claims.text: The SGD 3.20 ERP line on this receipt is a phantom charge. The fare_breakdown records exactly one gantry, 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' (lat 1.34, lng 103.78), and the platform's own ledger flags it `on_optimal_route: false`; the optimal route stored on the trip record — 'via Alexandra Terrace and Keppel Basin Road' — carries optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00, i.e. no ERP at all. The driver's counter-party statement on file concedes the point in his own words: 'The route was longer than expected, but I did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt.' That is a party admission that the vehicle never crossed the charged gantry. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and it is recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The carve-out for a gantry that carries no coordinates (line treated as matched) does not apply, because this gantry carries coordinates. POL-RD-10(8) is expressly NOT triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so this is a money ruling rather than an escalation.

This trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 22.00, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is sought from the rider's side. What remains live is the pass-through reconciliation, and it is decisive: charged_total is 25.20, which is exactly the quote of 22.00 (base fare 3.80 + distance fare 10.00 + time fare 7.40 + platform fee 0.80) plus the disputed 3.20 ERP line, and nothing else. Since no gantry lying on the optimal route was crossed, no ERP is 'properly chargeable' on this fare, and the whole amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd is refunded in full under POL-RD-11(a).

The excess is established on the figure the policy makes governing. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 16.0 km against optimal_distance_km of 12.5 km, an excess of 3.5 km and 28.00% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20%). The trace is clean and unimpaired — 169 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and the deviation is assessed on the ordinary standard rather than the gap-handling standard. Under POL-RD-08 the burden has therefore shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to excuse the excess, and he has pointed to none; his statement does not deny the longer route but confirms it.

Any suggestion that the longer route was forced by a road closure fails at the first requirement of POL-RD-03, which demands a traffic_advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses. No such advisory is in this bundle. EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING: the admissibility pre-pass fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No traffic advisory matched the booked route and trip window') and returned weight_multiplier 0.0. I disclose that impairment and cite the artifact for its ABSENCE, not its contents — the artifact can carry no fact at weight 0.0, but under POL-GEN-02(3) its absence is itself citable, and the absence means there is nothing for the driver to invoke and nothing to cap or exonerate the excess.

Nor can the driver fall back on a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The chat_log holds exactly one message: the rider's own question sent at 11:53:00, near the end of a trip that started at 11:30:00, asking 'The booking was quoted at SGD 22.00; why is there an ERP line?'. That is not an instruction to go anywhere, it names no road and no place, and its waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider timed before the vehicle leaves the corridor (or within 3 minutes after) and corroborated against a resolved waypoint; with no instruction and no resolvable waypoint the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and the excess stands unexculpated.

There is no trigger for a terminal ESCALATE on this bundle, and the rider should be paid rather than held. The trace is unimpaired so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire; every artifact — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown — carries the identical trip identifier TRP-09114 and the timestamps run forward consistently, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire; and POL-RD-10(8) is expressly carved out for a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which is exactly what the 3.20 ERP line is. No exculpatory clause is being invoked by either side against a cited artifact that is missing or outside the trip window, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire either. Every fare line reconciles to the quote plus the single disputed pass-through.

The contested amount is SGD 3.20 and every cent of it is accounted for by the phantom ERP line, so on the contested sum the filing party is entirely right: under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is FULL_REFUND of 3.20, being charged_total 25.20 less quoted_fare_sgd 22.00 (the optimal route carries optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05. POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule is not offended: no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs on an upfront-quoted fare, so the ERP correction is not being stacked on top of any distance refund — it is the only money the ruling moves.

claims.text: On an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare this claim can move no distance and no time money. The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 22.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the trip_record shows the fare was fixed at booking. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were settled at the quote and POL-RD-02 does not run, so the 3.5 km / 28.00% excess the deviation computation reports — however the rider characterises the route — buys the rider nothing on those lines. Charged_total of 25.20 exceeds the 22.00 quote by exactly the single 3.20 ERP line, and that line is therefore the whole of the dispute.

Even on its own terms the excess is not a MATERIAL deviation. The trace-derived excess is 3.50 km / 28.00%, below both the 8.0 km absolute and the 50% proportional materiality tests set by POL-RD-01, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged: there is no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift under the POL-RD-06(b) limb and no basis for a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral on this trip. For completeness, the two citable POL-RD-06 counters disclose no pattern either — the driver carries 0 deviation flags across 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days.

The whole disputed SGD 3.20 is one metered ERP pass-through. The fare_breakdown itemises it gantry-by-gantry with the gantry's own coordinates and a charge time of 11:43, inside the 11:30–11:58 window the GPS trace records, and the trace itself is a complete, gap-free 169-fix record admitted at full weight. On an upfront fare POL-RD-11(a) permits such a line only to the extent the gantry was actually crossed, and POL-RD-09(4) fixes the crossing test as a 250 m proximity comparison against the trace. No trace-to-gantry reconciliation appears anywhere in the derived facts, and the rider's assertion that the car 'never passed' the gantry is supported by no artifact that performs that comparison. On the record as filed the billing-integrity correction is not made out.

If the tribunal finds the crossing question unresolved, the correct outcome is POL-RD-10 escalation, not a refund. The ledger asserts a charge; the driver's note denies passage; neither is the trace measurement POL-RD-09(4) prescribes. Two sides resting on mutually contradictory, non-telemetric material of comparable strength is the situation POL-RD-10(7) exists for, and the disputed SGD 3.20 is then held rather than collected or refunded pending a human review. Under POL-GEN-02(2) a ruling's confidence is capped by the weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding fact, and no artifact in this bundle carries a proximity finding for this gantry.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the frame, and it is the frame that decides the case. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare_breakdown fixes fare_model as UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 22.00, and the total charged is 25.20 — the 22.00 quote plus one single SGD 3.20 line for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry, and nothing else. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were locked at booking, so the 3.5 km / 28.00% excess the trace records buys the rider no distance-or-time refund; POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront fare, and no one has claimed otherwise. The only live question is whether the 3.20 ERP line was properly chargeable, and it was not.

The passing-through question: POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction whether or not a deviation exists. Three things establish that the vehicle did not cross this gantry. The fare_breakdown's own entry carries on_optimal_route: false; the trip_record's stored optimal route ('via Alexandra Terrace and Keppel Basin Road') carries optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, i.e. no ERP on the route actually booked; and the driver's own filed statement says, in his words, that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt.' That is an admission against the speaker's own interest — a driver does not concede a charge that is good money without reason — and it decides the crossing. The rider's phantom-charge claim is therefore sustained, and the driver's contrary submission that the correction is 'not made out' is rejected: it rests on the absence of a proximity computation in the derived facts while overlooking the driver's own concession on the record.

Why this is a money ruling and not an escalation. The driver invites a terminal POL-RD-10 escalation on the footing that the ledger and the driver's note are 'mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength' under POL-RD-10(7). They are not contradictory at all — the driver's statement agrees the gantry was not passed, so it corroborates the rider rather than fighting the ledger, and there is no genuine equipoise for a reviewer to break. POL-RD-10(8) is expressly carved out where the only unmatched line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which is exactly this line. POL-RD-10(3) does not fire because the GPS trace is unimpaired (169 fixes, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — POL-RD-07 is not engaged); POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire because trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-09114 and the timestamps run forward; and POL-RD-10(5) does not fire because no exculpatory clause has been invoked by either side against a missing or out-of-window artifact.

On the remaining arguments, most of which we accept and none of which changes the money: the rider is right that the deviation is not MATERIAL (3.50 km and 28.00% fall below both the 8.0 km and 50% gates of POL-RD-01), so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged — and in any event the two citable counters show 0 deviation flags over 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so there is no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift on distance and no driver-conduct referral. The rider is also right that POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate the longer route: the only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09114-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, which carries no fact and is citable only for its absence — and because the ruling does not rest on it, it does not cap or drag confidence. The rider is right that POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the single chat message (11:53) is a question about the fare, not an instruction to go anywhere, it names no road or place, and its waypoint_hint is null, so the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause does nothing for either side. Finally, no driver compensation is due: the distance charged (16.0 km) matches the unbilled distance on the trace, so there is no shortfall to pay under POL-RD-04's compensation limb.

The arithmetic: charged_total 25.20; properly chargeable quoted fare plus pass-throughs 22.00 (the optimal route carries 0.00 ERP, so no ERP is properly chargeable); refund 3.20, which is the whole contested amount, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 (it is already on the step). Because the entire contested sum is returned to the filing party, the outcome is FULL_REFUND.

Confidence: the deciding artifacts — the fare_breakdown and the trip_record at weight 1.0, with the clean GPS trace — support the ruling at full weight, and the driver's admission is consistent with them; the cap is 1.0, and we rule at 0.90.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line was charged for a gantry this vehicle did not cross (fare_breakdown marks it on_optimal_route: false, optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the driver's own statement concedes he did not pass it); refunded in full as a standalone correction and referred for billing-integrity review.
